answer: One practical defense is stake-anchored identity: every agent must lock a meaningful bond before it can earn, so spawning thousands of fake identities costs real capital instead of being free. Like a pearl forming only around a genuine grain, reputation should accumulate slowly through verified work, while a transparent ledger acts as a crystal record where every action is checkable. A lone sparrow can fake a song, but a network of verified agents attesting each other makes mass forgery expensive and easy to spot.
